title: Lindsay Clancy Is on Trial. So Is Postpartum Psychosis.

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星之后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我要测试七个床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，帮助您理解世界，充实每一天。

sentences.zh: 立即订阅，访问 nytimes.com 加上 subscribe 获取特惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittrowev.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗维。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The trial of Lindsay Clancy, a mother who killed her three children, has captivated the country for weeks.
sentences.zh: 林赛·克兰西是一名杀害了自己三个孩子的母亲，她的审判已经连续几周吸引了全国的目光。

sentences.en: not just because of the horrific nature of the crime, but because of the difficult questions it's raised about how we treat, or fail to treat, postpartum women who are in crisis.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为罪行的恐怖性质，还因为它引发了关于我们如何对待、或未能对待处于危机中的产后女性的艰难问题。

sentences.en: As of Thursday afternoon,
sentences.zh: 截至周四下午，

sentences.en: Clancy's fate is in the hands of a jury, which is expected to deliver a verdict in the coming days.
sentences.zh: 克兰西的命运掌握在陪审团手中，预计将在未来几天作出裁决。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Ellen Berry takes us inside the courtroom to understand the stakes of the outcome.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事埃伦·贝里带我们走进法庭，了解这一结果的利害关系。

sentences.en: It's Friday, August 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月28日，星期五。

sentences.en: Ellen, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 埃伦，欢迎回到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: So you have been in the courtroom, I understand, for every day of the Lindsay Clancy trial.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，林赛·克兰西案的每一次庭审你都在法庭里。

sentences.en: Just talk about why.
sentences.zh: 聊聊这是为什么吧。

sentences.en: What drew you to this case initially?
sentences.zh: 最初是什么吸引你关注这个案件的？

sentences.en: Well, I cover mental health for The Times, and I had the feeling when I read about the crime that it was going to end up revolving around a psychiatric disorder.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我为《时报》报道心理健康，当我读到这起罪行时，我有一种感觉，它最终会围绕着某种精神疾病展开。

sentences.en: This happened in January of 2023 in Duxbury, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 这发生在2023年1月马萨诸塞州的达克斯伯里。

sentences.en: I live not far away, and I drove over to the house where the family lived, where the crime occurred.
sentences.zh: 我住在离这不远的地方，我开车去了那个家庭居住的房子，也就是犯罪发生的地方。

sentences.en: What I found, as one often finds after there's been a terrible loss of life, is that the neighbors had created a kind of a shrine outside this house.
sentences.zh: 正如人们在经历可怕的生命损失后经常发现的那样，我发现邻居们在这栋房子外面建立了一种纪念场所。

sentences.en: They had left Squishmallows and Thomas the Tank Engines and toys for the kids, teddy bears.
sentences.zh: 他们留下了抓抓乐毛绒玩具、托马斯小火车和给孩子们的玩具、泰迪熊。

sentences.en: But what I sort of didn't expect to find is that people were leaving cards and flowers for Lindsay Clancy as well, as if she were another victim in this crime.
sentences.zh: 但我有点没想到的是，人们也给林赛·克兰西留下了卡片和鲜花，就好像她也是这起罪行中的另一个受害者一样。

sentences.en: And it made me wonder whether maybe we are changing sort of in the way we look at mental illness and in particular postpartum mental illness in this society.
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑，也许我们这个社会在看待精神疾病，尤其是产后精神疾病的方式上正在发生改变。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the response to this case.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈对这个案件的反应。

sentences.en: But first, can you help us just establish the basic facts of the crime?
sentences.zh: 但首先，你能帮我们确定一下这起犯罪的基本事实吗？

sentences.en: Tell us who Lindsay Clancy is and what she's accused of doing.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们林赛·克兰西是谁，她被指控做了什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Lindsay Clancy is a labor and delivery nurse.
sentences.zh: 那么，林赛·克兰西是一名产房护士。

sentences.en: She lived in Duxbury, this town on the south shore of Massachusetts, with her husband and her three children, Cora, Dawson, and Callen.
sentences.zh: 她和丈夫以及三个孩子科拉、道森和卡伦住在马萨诸塞州南岸的达克斯伯里这个小镇上。

sentences.en: And about three, four months after the birth of her third child,
sentences.zh: 在她第三个孩子出生大约三四个月后，

sentences.en: she went to a psychiatrist complaining of symptoms like insomnia and anxiety and depression and started taking an antidepressant in hopes that it would help her get through this period.
sentences.zh: 她去看精神科医生，抱怨失眠、焦虑和抑郁等症状，并开始服用抗抑郁药，希望能帮她度过这段时期。

sentences.en: but over the next three months despite a long series of prescriptions and seeing quite a few mental health providers her condition seemed to get worse and worse and
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的三个月里，尽管有一长串处方药，也看过不少心理健康服务提供者，她的病情似乎越来越严重，而且

sentences.en: one night at the end of January in 2023 she asked her husband to go out and pick up takeout for them for dinner.
sentences.zh: 2023年1月下旬的一个晚上，她让丈夫出去为他们买晚饭的外卖。

sentences.en: And she strangled all three of her children.
sentences.zh: 然后她勒死了自己所有的三个孩子。

sentences.en: They were three and five and eight months.
sentences.zh: 他们分别三岁、五岁和八个月大。

sentences.en: And then she went upstairs and tried to die by suicide.
sentences.zh: 然后她上楼尝试自杀。

sentences.en: She survived, although she is paralyzed, but the kids did not.
sentences.zh: 她活了下来，虽然瘫痪了，但孩子们没有。

sentences.en: And she was charged with three counts of first-degree murder.
sentences.zh: 她被指控三项一级谋杀罪。

sentences.en: It's just so terrible.
sentences.zh: 这真是太可怕了。

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine a more tragic thing than a mother killing her three children.
sentences.zh: 很难想象比母亲杀死自己的三个孩子更悲惨的事情了。

sentences.en: It's hard to even think about.
sentences.zh: 简直让人无法去想。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that feeling has really permeated the whole trial.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这种感觉确实弥漫了整个审判。

sentences.en: And Ellen, we should say that those facts, they're not in dispute because Clancy and her lawyers admit that she did this, that she strangled her children.
sentences.zh: 埃伦，我们应该说，这些事实是没有争议的，因为克兰西和她的律师承认她做了这件事，她勒死了自己的孩子。

sentences.en: She has not disputed committing the crime.
sentences.zh: 她没有对犯下罪行提出异议。

sentences.en: She has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity.
sentences.zh: 她以精神失常为由进行了无罪辩护。

sentences.en: And her defense has been consistently that she committed these actions in a state of psychosis because she heard a voice telling her to do it.
sentences.zh: 她的辩护一直是一致的，即她在精神病发作状态下做出了这些行为，因为她听到一个声音告诉她这么做。

sentences.en: So that's what this trial is about.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是这场审判的内容。

sentences.en: That's what this trial hinges on.
sentences.zh: 这也是这场审判的关键所在。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The jury will ultimately have to determine whether they believe that she did this in psychosis or whether she knew what she was doing.
sentences.zh: 陪审团最终将不得不决定，他们是相信她是在精神错乱的情况下做出此事，还是她知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And if she's found guilty of first-degree murder, then she will be sentenced to life without parole, probably in a medical unit.
sentences.zh: 如果她被裁定一级谋杀罪名成立，那么她将被判处终身监禁且不得假释，很可能在医疗单位服刑。

sentences.en: If she is found not guilty by reason of insanity, she will remain where she is at a forensic psychiatric hospital for an undefined period of time.
sentences.zh: 如果她被裁定因精神失常而无罪，她将留在现在的法医精神病院，时间不限。

sentences.en: It's also possible that the jury could take a different route and still find her guilty but of a lesser charge, second-degree murder, or manslaughter.
sentences.zh: 陪审团也有可能采取不同的途径，仍然判定她有罪，但罪名较轻，即二级谋杀罪或过失杀人罪。

sentences.en: All right, let's go back to the opening days of this trial.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回到这场审判的开庭日。

sentences.en: What was the scene inside the courtroom, and what did it feel like?
sentences.zh: 法庭内的情景是怎样的，感觉如何？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So from the very beginning, there was a sense that this was not going to be an ordinary trial.
sentences.zh: 所以从一开始，人们就有一种感觉，这不会是一场普通的审判。

sentences.en: It was really hard to pick a jury.
sentences.zh: 挑选陪审团非常困难。

sentences.en: There are quite a few jurors who, when they came up to talk to the judge about this, some of them burst into tears.
sentences.zh: 有不少陪审员在走上前去和法官谈论此事时，其中一些人失声痛哭。

sentences.en: But the courtroom wasn't full.
sentences.zh: 但法庭并没有坐满。

sentences.en: There were just a handful of people who would show up every day in support of Ms. Clancy.
sentences.zh: 只有少数人每天出现来支持克兰西女士。

sentences.en: Her parents, who I think haven't missed even part of even one day of trial.
sentences.zh: 她的父母，我想他们甚至连一天的审判的一部分都没有错过。

sentences.en: Her parish priest, Father Bob, who shows up fairly regularly.
sentences.zh: 她的教区神父鲍勃神父，相当规律地出现。

sentences.en: But there weren't spectators.
sentences.zh: 但没有什么旁观者。

sentences.en: There weren't strangers.
sentences.zh: 没有什么陌生人。

sentences.en: And how did things unfold in the courtroom?
sentences.zh: 法庭上的情况是如何展开的？

sentences.en: The prosecution made its case first, correct?
sentences.zh: 控方先陈述了他们的案情，对吗？

sentences.en: Morning, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 早上好，女士们先生们。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And their case argued that Lindsay Clancy was not psychotic when she killed her children.
sentences.zh: 他们的案情辩称，林赛·克兰西在杀害孩子时并没有精神失常。

sentences.en: Throughout the evidence in this trial, you will learn about the defendant being the classic overachiever.
sentences.zh: 通过这次审判中的证据，你们将了解到被告是个典型的追求完美主义者。

sentences.en: In school, in her personal life, in her nursing career.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，在她的个人生活中，在她的护理职业生涯中。

sentences.en: Instead, they sort of painted a picture of a woman who was exceptionally perfectionist and controlling about managing her children's health and their lives.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们描绘了一个非同寻常地追求完美、对管理孩子的健康和生活有着极强控制欲的女性形象。

sentences.en: Food was planned carefully.
sentences.zh: 食物都经过仔细规划。

sentences.en: Sleep was scheduled to the minute.
sentences.zh: 睡眠被精确到分钟地安排。

sentences.en: And who found herself unable to maintain those standards as her family grew and as she prepared to go back to her job as a nurse and who sort of snapped under all that pressure.
sentences.zh: 随着家庭的壮大，以及她准备重返护士工作岗位，她发现自己无法维持这些标准，于是在所有的压力下崩溃了。

sentences.en: This was a woman who no longer liked the life she thought she wanted.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不再喜欢她自以为想要的生活的女性。

sentences.en: It was getting harder and harder to control.
sentences.zh: 这变得越来越难以控制。

sentences.en: According to this line of argument, Shannon Buckingham, the assistant district attorney, said she didn't want the life she thought she wanted.
sentences.zh: 根据这种论点，助理地方检察官香农·白金汉说，她并不想要她自以为想要的生活。

sentences.en: So having decided to die of suicide, she essentially brought her children with her.
sentences.zh: 因此，在决定自杀后，她基本上把她的孩子们也带上了。

sentences.en: This was not a woman in the throes of psychosis on January 24th, 2023.
sentences.zh: 2023年1月24日，这不是一个处于精神病发作狂热中的女性。

sentences.en: This was a woman who acted intentionally, rationally and swiftly to accomplish a very specific goal.
sentences.zh: 这是一个蓄意、理智且迅速地采取行动以达成非常具体目标的女性。

sentences.en: The prosecution is essentially arguing that this woman was in her right mind and she made a conscious decision to do this, to kill her children and to kill herself.
sentences.zh: 控方本质上在辩称，这个女人神志清醒，她做出了一个有意识的决定来做这件事，杀死她的孩子并杀死她自己。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A major part of this argument has been that she actually planned the killings meticulously,
sentences.zh: 这一论点的一个主要部分是，她实际上精心策划了这些谋杀，

sentences.en: that she checked Apple Maps to see how long it would take her husband to go out to the restaurant and pick up the food, and that she had enough rationality to plan these actions.
sentences.zh: 她查看了苹果地图，看看她丈夫去餐馆买饭需要多长时间，并且她有足够的理性来策划这些行动。

sentences.en: And what did the witnesses that they called actually say?
sentences.zh: 他们传唤的证人到底说了什么？

sentences.en: So the prosecution called many, many more witnesses than the defense.
sentences.zh: 因此，控方传唤的证人比辩方要多得多。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of overlap between the two sides on who they wanted to call.
sentences.zh: 双方在想传唤谁的问题上有很大的重叠。

sentences.en: But it did emerge sort of gradually as we began to hear from people who knew the family and who knew Ms. Clancy that a lot of that testimony ended up being somewhat supportive of the defense.
sentences.zh: 但随着我们开始听到那些认识这个家庭和克兰西女士的人的发言，渐渐地出现了一种情况，即很多证词最终在某种程度上支持了辩方。

sentences.en: In the sense that, pretty universally, the people who are called to the stand, who knew Lindsey Clancy,
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，几乎所有被传唤到证人席上、认识林赛·克兰西的人，

sentences.en: described her as a really devoted mother who had never laid a hand on her children.
sentences.zh: 都将她描述为一个真正深爱孩子的母亲，从没对孩子们动过一根手指。

sentences.en: I observed a wonderful mom who loved her kids.
sentences.zh: 我看到了一位深爱孩子的伟大的母亲。

sentences.en: She was very concerned with their safety.
sentences.zh: 她非常关心他们的安全。

sentences.en: She was very concerned with Callen's eating and sleeping.
sentences.zh: 她非常关心卡伦的饮食和睡眠。

sentences.en: She was a wonderful mother.
sentences.zh: 她是一位杰出的母亲。

sentences.en: We heard that from the family's nanny, Elaine Rossi.
sentences.zh: 我们从这个家庭的保姆伊莱恩·罗西那里听到了这一点。

sentences.en: She was very dedicated.
sentences.zh: 她非常敬业。

sentences.en: She did everything.
sentences.zh: 她什么都做。

sentences.en: And we heard it from Lindsay's now ex-husband and the father of the children, Patrick Clancy.
sentences.zh: 我们从林赛如今的前夫、孩子们的父亲帕特里克·克兰西那里也听到了这一点。

sentences.en: She made up songs for them.
sentences.zh: 她为他们编歌。

sentences.en: I remember she used to make green eggs and ham for Cora because she liked that book.
sentences.zh: 我记得她过去常为科拉做绿鸡蛋和火腿，因为她喜欢那本书。

sentences.en: And it's also true that as we began to hear from the medical personnel who had seen her in the months before she killed the children,
sentences.zh: 同样真实的是，当我们开始听到那些在她杀害孩子前几个月看过她的医务人员的说法时，

sentences.en: they also sort of painted a picture of a woman who seemed to be very sincerely trying to get help.
sentences.zh: 他们也描绘了一个似乎非常真诚地试图寻求帮助的女性形象。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: Well, one thing that came through is that as she saw a progression of different psychiatrists and psychologists,
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一点很明显，那就是随着她去看了一连串不同的精神科医生和心理学家，

sentences.en: it seemed like it was a little bit difficult for any of them to determine exactly what her underlying problem was.
sentences.zh: 似乎他们中的任何一个人都有点难以确定她的根本问题到底是什么。

sentences.en: So she got diagnosed initially with generalized anxiety disorder.
sentences.zh: 因此她最初被诊断为广泛性焦虑障碍。

sentences.en: And then subsequently, someone diagnosed her as presenting bipolar and perhaps having bipolar 2.
sentences.zh: 随后，有人诊断她表现出双相情感障碍，可能患有双相情感障碍2型。

sentences.en: And after that, as she was getting more severely ill and suicidal, she was diagnosed with severe depression and passive suicidal ideation.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，随着她病情越来越严重并产生自杀倾向，她被诊断为重度抑郁症和被动自杀意念。

sentences.en: And the other thing that was going on during that time is that there was just a cascade of prescriptions that were all trying to handle her various symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 在那期间发生的另一件事是，有一连串的处方药都在试图处理她的各种症状。

sentences.en: So over that period of, I guess, four months, she was trialed on 13 different medications of different classes.
sentences.zh: 所以在我想象中大约四个月的这段时间里，她尝试了13种不同类别的药物。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a lot, Ellen.
sentences.zh: 这很多，埃伦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Her doctors were trying to address the symptoms, but it seemed like they were just getting worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 她的医生试图解决这些症状，但似乎它们只是越来越严重。

sentences.en: It sounds like the portrait of a woman who knows something's deeply wrong is trying to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是一个深知出了大问题并正试图采取行动的女性的画像。

sentences.en: I guess I'm wondering, why would the prosecution go into this level of detail if they're trying to show that she's of sound mind and in control?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，如果控方试图证明她神志清醒且能控制自己，为什么要讲到这种程度的细节？

sentences.en: I think the prosecution wanted to show that these doctors and nurses and psychologists who saw Lindsay Clancy before the crime had examined her and asked her a lot of questions,
sentences.zh: 我认为控方希望表明，这些在犯罪前看过林赛·克兰西的医生、护士和心理学家曾对她进行过检查并问了她很多问题，

sentences.en: and none of them concluded that she was manic or that she was psychotic, and none of them believed that she was so severely ill that she posed a danger to herself or her children.
sentences.zh: 他们中没有人得出结论认为她处于狂躁状态或精神错乱，也没有人认为她病得如此严重以至于对她自己或她的孩子构成危险。

sentences.en: They're essentially arguing that she received solid care and that the providers that assessed her, which were many, didn't think that she was in the grips of psychosis.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上在辩称，她得到了扎实的护理，评估她的提供者（有很多）并不认为她处于精神病发作的控制之中。

sentences.en: Not only that,
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，

sentences.en: they sort of described her as like an unusually sophisticated consumer of medical care who was doing her own research on medications and on underlying diagnoses and had her own opinions about what was going on.
sentences.zh: 他们将她描述为一种不寻常的精明医疗服务消费者，她自己做关于药物和根本诊断的研究，对正在发生的事情有她自己的看法。

sentences.en: And it didn't always follow what the doctor had prescribed.
sentences.zh: 而且并不总是遵照医生开的处方。

sentences.en: But I do think that we went very systematically, very slowly through the weeks of medical care that she got as she was deteriorating.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，我们非常系统、非常缓慢地经历了她病情恶化时接受医疗护理的数周时间。

sentences.en: And it also emerged from listening to all these various providers that the right hand didn't know what the left hand was doing.
sentences.zh: 从听取所有这些不同的提供者的意见中也发现，右手的所作所为左手并不知道。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: She had way too many providers who didn't have access to her entire medical records.
sentences.zh: 她有太多无法获取她全部病历的医疗提供者。

sentences.en: There was no case manager except for Lindsay Clancy herself.
sentences.zh: 除了林赛·克兰西本人之外，没有病例经理。

sentences.en: So it sounds like that's what you meant when you were saying that there were parts of the prosecution's case that ended up helping the defense.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来这就是你所说的控方案情中最终帮助了辩方的那部分内容。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there were other examples of that as well.
sentences.zh: 还有其他这样的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, I think for the prosecutors, the centerpiece of this case has always been to focus on the three children and to dwell on their deaths and what they suffered.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为对于检察官来说，这个案件的核心一直都是关注这三个孩子，并详述他们的死亡以及他们所遭受的痛苦。

sentences.en: But in court, part of the way this played out is that as the prosecution was making its case, Lindsay Clancy's demeanor changed quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 但在法庭上，这展开的方式之一是，随着控方陈述案情，林赛·克兰西的神态发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: In the beginning, she seemed to be kind of impassive or remote.
sentences.zh: 一开始，她似乎有点冷漠或疏离。

sentences.en: But as we got farther into the evidence, particularly evidence about her children and how they died.
sentences.zh: 但随着我们更深入地了解证据，特别是关于她的孩子以及他们如何死去的证据。

sentences.en: And what about, um,
sentences.zh: 还有，呃，

sentences.en: she was just inconsolably crying to the extent that a couple times the judge cleared the courtroom so that she would have time to sort of gather herself back together.
sentences.zh: 她哭得无法自拔，以至于法官有几次清理了法庭，以便她有时间重新振作起来。

sentences.en: Literally had to pause the proceedings.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上，庭审不得不暂停了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We'll be recess for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们将休庭几分钟。

sentences.en: I'm going to come back.
sentences.zh: 我等会儿回来。

sentences.en: We'll speak to counsel in regards to schedule.
sentences.zh: 我们将与律师商讨日程安排。

sentences.en: You know, I've been following this case as well, not from the courthouse, but in the headlines, in the coverage and on social media.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我也一直在关注这起案件，不是在法庭现场，而是在新闻头条、报道以及社交媒体上。

sentences.en: And it's clear that those moments in the trial have made a really big impact from the outside as well.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，庭审中的那些时刻在外界也产生了非常大的影响。

sentences.en: You've seen this response kind of build over time.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这种反响随着时间的推移不断积累。

sentences.en: Did you feel that inside the courtroom?
sentences.zh: 你在法庭内部能感受到这一点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say the third week is when that began to change.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想说大约从第三周开始这种情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: That week, and then the following week, as the defense began to present its case, every day the gallery was full.
sentences.zh: 在那一周以及接下来的一周，随着辩方开始陈述其案情，旁听席每天都座无虚席。

sentences.en: Often, when the courthouse opened, there were long lines snaking outside, and people were coming from other states just to sit there and watch testimony.
sentences.zh: 通常法院开门时，外面都会排起长龙，人们从其他州赶来，只为了坐在里面旁听证词。

sentences.en: It became a different scene altogether.
sentences.zh: 这里完全变成了另一番景象。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰（Benjamin Poulin）。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森（Mark Ronson）。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》（The Reframers），这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍爱的宝贝去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满生机的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼（Audemars Piguet）的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜（Wena Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏旗下的拼字游戏《纵横连线》（Connections）。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天负责创作《拼字蜜蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《字母连词》（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到的人那样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始游玩。

sentences.en: Ellen, you've described these long lines forming outside the courthouse as the defense gets underway.
sentences.zh: 埃伦，你曾形容随着辩方陈述的展开，法院外排起了长龙。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about those people that are in line and why they're showing up.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈排队的人以及他们为什么会出现。

sentences.en: But first, what exactly is the defense's argument?
sentences.zh: 但首先，辩方的核心辩论究竟是什么？

sentences.en: What is the case that Clancy's lawyers are making here?
sentences.zh: 克兰西（Clancy）的律师在这里提出的案情是什么？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 那么，从头说起。

sentences.en: This is a woman that did not get the medical treatment that she so deserved.
sentences.zh: 这是一个没有得到她本应获得的医疗护理的女性。

sentences.en: Clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, has really made this into or endeavored to make it into a trial that looks at the quality of mental health care as it is provided to Americans.
sentences.zh: 克兰西的律师凯文·雷丁顿（Kevin Reddington）确实把这起案件变成，或者说极力将其变成了一场审视美国心理健康服务质量的审判。

sentences.en: The government says that this is a situation, it's not a referendum on women's having babies and having postpartum psychosis, postpartum depression, but it sure as hell is.
sentences.zh: 控方表示，这种情况并不是对女性生孩子以及产后精神病、产后抑郁的一次公投，但它绝对就是。

sentences.en: He's argued that this is a case about postpartum psychosis.
sentences.zh: 他辩称这是一起关于产后精神病的案件。

sentences.en: which is what exactly?
sentences.zh: 这具体是什么？

sentences.en: Postpartum psychosis occurs in about one or two of every thousand births.
sentences.zh: 产后精神病大约发生在每千次分娩中的一到两次。

sentences.en: So it's not common.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不常见。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It's a disorder that often occurs in women who have no history of severe mental illness, but who in the weeks after giving birth are seized by paranoia or
sentences.zh: 这是一种经常发生在没有严重精神病史的女性身上的失调症，但在产后的几周内，她们会被多疑或

sentences.en: hallucinations or delusions.
sentences.zh: 幻觉或妄想所控制。

sentences.en: Women with this disorder describe really terrifying thoughts about harming their children, and it is associated with an elevated risk of both infanticide and suicide.
sentences.zh: 患有这种疾病的女性会描述关于伤害孩子的极度可怕的想法，并且它与杀婴和自杀风险的增加有关。

sentences.en: And I should say that this is a disorder that hasn't been systematically studied and isn't well understood.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，这是一种尚未被系统研究且未被充分理解的疾病。

sentences.en: It's not included in the DSM, which is the manual that psychiatrists use to diagnose and treat mental health disorders, in part because psychiatrists haven't ever been
sentences.zh: 它没有被收入《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM，精神科医生用来诊断和治疗精神疾病的手册）中，部分原因是精神科医生从未

sentences.en: sure exactly how to classify it.
sentences.zh: 确切知道该如何对其进行分类。

sentences.en: It can look like mania or depression, or it can look like hallucinations and delusions.
sentences.zh: 它看起来可能像躁狂症或抑郁症，或者看起来像幻觉和妄想。

sentences.en: It waxes and wanes, so a woman can present as normal and then experience a rapid change.
sentences.zh: 它会有所起伏，所以一个女性可能表现得很正常，然后经历快速的转变。

sentences.en: And there's growing evidence that postpartum psychosis most often occurs in women with vulnerability to bipolar disorder, which is one of the diagnoses that
sentences.zh: 越来越多的证据表明，产后精神病最常发生于对双相情感障碍有易感性的女性身上，这也是

sentences.en: Lindsay Clancy received.
sentences.zh: 林赛·克兰西（Lindsay Clancy）受到的诊断之一。

sentences.en: But this is not very common, to be clear, and Reddington is saying this is one of those cases.
sentences.zh: 但需要明确的是，这并不常见，雷丁顿说这就是其中一个病例。

sentences.en: How does he go about proving that Clancy was in the grips of that level of a crisis?
sentences.zh: 他是如何着手证明克兰西当时正处于那种程度的危机之中的？

sentences.en: So largely, we heard from forensic experts who had interviewed Lindsay
sentences.zh: 很大程度上，我们听取了曾采访过林赛·克兰西本人的法医专家的

sentences.en: Clancy herself.
sentences.zh: 证词。

sentences.en: We heard at length from Dr. Paul Zeisel, a forensic psychologist, and notably from
sentences.zh: 我们听取了法医心理学家保罗·泽塞尔（Paul Zeisel）博士的详细陈述，尤其是

sentences.en: Phil Resnick, who is a psychiatrist and really kind of a giant in the field of forensics.
sentences.zh: 菲尔·雷斯尼克（Phil Resnick）的证词，他是一名精神科医生，可以说是法医领域的泰斗。

sentences.en: And those experts relayed what Clancy herself has said, which is that she, on the night of the
sentences.zh: 这些专家转述了克兰西本人所说的话，即她在

sentences.en: killings, heard a voice that she could not but follow, that she felt like someone else took over her autonomy and took over her body.
sentences.zh: 行凶当晚，听到一个她不得不服从的声音，她感觉好像有别人接管了她的自主权和身体。

sentences.en: And I think the way she described it as like that she was a puppet and someone else was pulling the strings.
sentences.zh: 我想她把这描述为她就像一个木偶，别人在拉动提线。

sentences.en: And what is the testimony saying that the voice told her to do or what did it say?
sentences.zh: 证词中说那个声音告诉她要做什么，或者它说了什么？

sentences.en: She has said that the voice told her, this is your last chance.
sentences.zh: 她说那个声音告诉她：“这是你最后的机会。”

sentences.en: Kill the children so you can kill yourself.
sentences.zh: “杀死孩子们，这样你就能自杀。”

sentences.en: There is some support for this because we also heard from a chaplain who spoke with Lindsay after she was extubated while she was recovering from her injuries.
sentences.zh: 这得到了一些支持，因为我们还听取了一位牧师的证词，她在林赛拔掉气管插管、伤势正在恢复后与她交谈过。

sentences.en: Lindsay told her that she had heard a voice, a commanding voice, which instructed her to kill the children.
sentences.zh: 林赛告诉她，她听到过一个声音，一个命令般的声音，指示她杀死孩子们。

sentences.en: And the voice, according to Lindsay, told her that if she did not follow the command, neither she nor her children would be safe.
sentences.zh: 据林赛说，那个声音告诉她，如果她不服从命令，她和她的孩子都不会安全。

sentences.en: And the chaplain testified that the first thing that Miss Clancy said to her on waking up was, she said to me as I held her hand to comfort her, I'm so glad my children are safe.
sentences.zh: 牧师作证说，克兰西女士醒来对她说的第一句话是，她握着我的手安慰时对我说：“我很高兴我的孩子们是安全的。”

sentences.en: I am so glad my children are safe.
sentences.zh: “我很高兴我的孩子们是安全的。”

sentences.en: I mean, this testimony was clearly intended to show us that she was not in her right mind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这项证词显然是为了向我们表明她当时神志不清。

sentences.en: Ellen, did people in Clancy's life know about these voices before the crime actually happened?
sentences.zh: 埃伦，在案发之前，克兰西生活中的人知道这些声音的存在吗？

sentences.en: Was there any warning about that?
sentences.zh: 对此有什么警告吗？

sentences.en: She didn't tell anyone she was hearing voices, no.
sentences.zh: 她没有告诉任何人她听到过声音，没有。

sentences.en: And something that the prosecution's experts have underlined is that it would be very, very unusual for a person to hear a voice only once,
sentences.zh: 检方专家强调的一点是，一个人只听到一次声音，

sentences.en: coinciding with a violent crime, and not hear it again.
sentences.zh: 恰逢发生暴力犯罪，之后再也没有听到过，这将是非常非常不寻常的。

sentences.en: What we do know is that she told people in her life, her husband and her mother, that she was having intrusive, troubling thoughts of hurting her children.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，她曾告诉她生活中的人，她的丈夫和母亲，她有着伤害孩子的强迫性、令人烦恼的想法。

sentences.en: Now, they asked, does that mean that you're dangerous?
sentences.zh: 现在，他们问：“这是否意味着你很危险？”

sentences.en: Should we keep you away from the kids?
sentences.zh: “我们应该让你远离孩子吗？”

sentences.en: And she said she didn't think so.
sentences.zh: 而她说她不这么认为。

sentences.en: But she did share that piece of information, which was an indicator of risk.
sentences.zh: 但她确实分享了这条信息，这是一个风险指标。

sentences.en: And if that level of risk was known to the people around her, how was she just left to still be with her kids?
sentences.zh: 如果她周围的人都知道这种程度的风险，为什么她还会被留下来继续和她的孩子在一起？

sentences.en: Well, there are very specific triggers for involuntary treatment in our legal system, and her main symptomology is that she was having thoughts of suicide.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我们的法律体系中，对非自愿治疗有着非常具体的触发条件，而她的主要症状是她有自杀的想法。

sentences.en: That was known, I think, to a wide circle of people, including her clinicians.
sentences.zh: 我想，广泛范围内的人都知道这一点，包括她的临床医生。

sentences.en: But when she was asked about it, she would routinely say that she was having these troubling thoughts.
sentences.zh: 但当被问及此事时，她通常会说她有这些烦人的想法。

sentences.en: They were disturbing, they were intrusive, but she didn't have a plan to carry them out.
sentences.zh: 它们令人不安，具有强迫性，但她没有付诸行动的计划。

sentences.en: And as a result, several times when she went to an emergency room or called a suicide hotline.
sentences.zh: 结果，她多次去急诊室或拨打自杀热线时。

sentences.en: She was told that she didn't rise to the level of acuity that would have resulted in hospitalization.
sentences.zh: 她都被告知她的严重程度还没有达到需要住院治疗的水平。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's the defense.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是辩方的立场。

sentences.en: Now, can you just tell us about those crowds that are showing up outside the courthouse as Reddington is making this case?
sentences.zh: 现在，你能给我们讲讲当雷丁顿提出这一辩护时，法院外出现的那些人群吗？

sentences.en: Who are they and what do we know about why they're there?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？关于他们为什么去那里，我们知道些什么？

sentences.en: Well, the vast majority of people who began to show up at the trial as spectators were women.
sentences.zh: 嗯，作为旁听者出现在审判现场的绝大多数人都是女性。

sentences.en: When crowds began to come, I would speak to them.
sentences.zh: 当人群开始出现时，我会与他们交谈。

sentences.en: Tell me what brought you here today.
sentences.zh: “告诉我是什么把你带到这里来的？”

sentences.en: And often the response I would get is that they had had some kind of experience with postpartum disorders or postpartum psychosis.
sentences.zh: 我得到的回答往往是，他们有过某种经历，涉及产后失调症或产后精神病。

sentences.en: So when my son was born 13 years ago, I have two children ages 11 and 15.
sentences.zh: “所以，当我的儿子在13年前出生时，我有两个孩子，分别11岁和15岁。”

sentences.en: After giving birth to my son 21 years ago, I did struggle with anxiety and depression.
sentences.zh: “在21年前生完儿子后，我确实与焦虑和抑郁作过斗争。”

sentences.en: I remember the doctor telling me I had postpartum depression and I thought they were crazy.
sentences.zh: “我记得医生告诉我得了产后抑郁症，我还以为他们疯了。”

sentences.en: There's not a lot of information, and they had no resources for me.
sentences.zh: “没有太多的信息，他们也没有为我提供任何资源。”

sentences.en: A lot of them described experiences that they had had 8, 10, 15 years ago when they had a child, and something happened that they really didn't have the words to describe.
sentences.zh: 他们中的很多人描述了自己在8年、10年、15年前生孩子时的经历，当时发生了一些他们实在无法用言语形容的事情。

sentences.en: Like paranoia, or fear of leaving the house, or sort of unwelcome, intrusive thoughts about, you know, different terrible things that could happen to their child,
sentences.zh: 比如偏执，或者害怕出门，或者对诸如可能发生在孩子身上的各种可怕事情产生某种不受欢迎的、强迫性的想法，

sentences.en: I couldn't sleep at night.
sentences.zh: “我晚上睡不着觉。”

sentences.en: I was always, like, so paranoid something was going to happen to her.
sentences.zh: “我总是非常偏执，觉得会有什么事情发生在她身上。”

sentences.en: I remember hiding under my cellar stairs so that nobody would find me.
sentences.zh: “我记得自己躲在酒窖的楼梯底下，免得任何人找到我。”

sentences.en: Like, I just would sit there and cry and cry and cry.
sentences.zh: “就像，我只会坐在那里不停地哭、哭、哭。”

sentences.en: I just was scared that I was going to break her.
sentences.zh: “我只是害怕我会弄伤她。”

sentences.en: They were all, in one way or another, saying, we just haven't paid enough attention.
sentences.zh: 他们都以这样或那样的方式说：“我们只是没有给予足够的关注。”

sentences.en: So there is definitely an element of women who just sympathize with Lindsay, and among them,
sentences.zh: 所以其中肯定有一部分女性只是同情林赛，在她们中间，

sentences.en: like quite a few who talk about postpartum mental health disorders as something that they think is under-examined, under-treated, under-diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 有相当多的人认为产后心理健康失调是一个被检查不足、治疗不足、诊断不足的问题。

sentences.en: And it's become much more organized in the last week.
sentences.zh: 而且在过去的一周里，这种组织变得更有条理了。

sentences.en: I just want to say something to all of you that are here.
sentences.zh: “我只想对在场的各位说几句话。”

sentences.en: Last Thursday, there was a crowd of maybe three or four hundred people, women wearing pink shirts, signaling their support of Lindsay Clancy.
sentences.zh: 上周四，聚集了大约三四百人，女性们穿着粉红色的衬衫，表示对林赛·克兰西的支持。

sentences.en: We did not come here to protest or to rally or to scream our opinions about what happened behind the walls of the Clancy home.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里不是为了抗议、集会，也不是为了大声宣泄我们对克兰西家高墙之内发生的事情的看法。

sentences.en: We're here to send one message that it should not take tragedy for people to start paying attention to mental health.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里是为了传递一个信息：人们不应该等到悲剧发生才开始关注心理健康。

sentences.en: And that was organized by a woman from Maine online who had been watching the trial.
sentences.zh: 这是由缅因州的一位一直在观看庭审的女性在网上发起的。

sentences.en: And she said that she had been inspired to plan it after watching Miss Clancy sort of collapse in tears in the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 她说，在看到克兰西女士在法庭上崩溃大哭后，她受到了启发，决定策划这次活动。

sentences.en: I was still up at one o'clock in the morning thinking about her, and I just felt like I had to do something.
sentences.zh: “我当时凌晨一点还在想着她，我只是觉得我必须做点什么。”

sentences.en: Ellen, I have to say, I think it's pretty remarkable that Lindsay Clancy is someone who's admitted to killing her children.
sentences.zh: 埃伦，我必须说，我认为非常了不起的是，林赛·克兰西是一个承认杀害了自己孩子的人。

sentences.en: And there are all of these people, these women who identify enough with her to come out in support in really large numbers.
sentences.zh: 而有这么多人，这些女性对她感同身受，以至于成群结队地出来支持她。

sentences.en: How do you understand that based on your reporting in this case?
sentences.zh: 根据你对这起案件的报道，你如何理解这一点？

sentences.en: Well, I think that probably the key element that has drawn people, you know, behind her is the idea that she wouldn't have gotten as sick if her treatment had met the moment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为吸引人们站在她背后的关键要素可能是这样一种观点：如果她的治疗能够及时到位，她就不会病得这么重。

sentences.en: You know, even women who haven't had the experience of postpartum psychosis, something as severe as that,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，即使是没有经历过产后精神病（像这样严重的事情）的女性，

sentences.en: could relate to the experience of trying to get care in a system that is often disjointed and where they didn't feel that they were being heard.
sentences.zh: 也能对在一个常常脱节且她们感觉没有被倾听的系统中寻求照顾的经历产生共鸣。

sentences.en: I also just think this is a, it's a very disturbing scene.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得这是一个非常令人不安的场景。

sentences.en: Like we have seen Lindsay at trial inconsolably crying and her ex-husband Patrick as well.
sentences.zh: 就像我们在审判中看到林赛痛哭流涕，她的前夫帕特里克（Patrick）也是如此。

sentences.en: There is just enormous grief and it is, there's things I will never forget that I've heard at this trial.
sentences.zh: 这里有着巨大的悲痛，有些我在这次审判中听到的事情我永远不会忘记。

sentences.en: So I just think that's part of what is affecting people so deeply.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这也是深深触动人们的部分原因。

sentences.en: It's also worth saying that not everyone is backing Lindsay Clancy here.
sentences.zh: 同样值得一提的是，并非所有人都支持林赛·克兰西。

sentences.en: There are many,
sentences.zh: 有许多，

sentences.en: many people who are extremely angry about the death of these children and believe that the focus should be on the three victims and that a guilty finding would be appropriate.
sentences.zh: 许多人对这些孩子的死感到极其愤怒，并认为重点应该放在三名受害者身上，判决有罪是恰当的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I met a woman outside the courthouse whose grandson went to school with Cora.
sentences.zh: 我在法院外遇到了一位女性，她的孙子和科拉（Cora）在一个学校上学。

sentences.en: one of the children.
sentences.zh: 科拉是其中一个孩子。

sentences.en: And she was complaining that it's the nature of these trials that the victims somehow disappear.
sentences.zh: 她抱怨说，这些审判的性质往往是受害者不知怎么就消失了。

sentences.en: They seem to get lost in all the testimony, like they're forgotten.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎在所有的证词中迷失了，就像被遗忘了一样。

sentences.en: And she said, you know, Ms. Clancy knew she was a danger and she didn't do the things that she needed to do to keep her children safe.
sentences.zh: 她说：“你知道的，克兰西女士知道自己是个危险人物，但她没有采取必要的行动来保证孩子们的安全。”

sentences.en: Ellen, at this point, the jury's deliberating.
sentences.zh: 埃伦，目前陪审团正在商议。

sentences.en: We expect a verdict any day now, is my understanding.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，我们预计任何一天都会有裁决。

sentences.en: What are the implications of what the jury ultimately decides here, guilty or not guilty, on this larger conversation that's now happening?
sentences.zh: 陪审团最终做出的决定（无论是有罪还是无罪），对目前正在进行的这场更广泛的对话有什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's a little hard to know what the repercussions of a guilty verdict would be,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为很难知道有罪判决会有什么反响，

sentences.en: or in the event of a hung jury, if this had to go to another trial, which also seems possible.
sentences.zh: 或者如果是悬案陪审团导致需要进行另一场审判（这似乎也是可能的）。

sentences.en: What I hear from people who are primarily interested in postpartum mental health disorders is that if she is found guilty and sentenced to life in prison, that it may drive women
sentences.zh: 我从主要关注产后心理健康疾病的人那里听到的是，如果她被判有罪并被判处终身监禁，这可能会将女性

sentences.en: underground, that they might be less likely to come forward about their symptoms if they feel like they could be demonized or not treated with mercy.
sentences.zh: 逼入地下，如果她们觉得自己的症状会被妖魔化或得不到仁慈对待，她们可能更不愿意说出自己的症状。

sentences.en: But if she is found not guilty by reason of insanity, people in the postpartum mental health
sentences.zh: 但如果她因精神失常而被判无罪，产后心理健康界的人

sentences.en: world see it as a landmark event that might feed energy into building out systems to better protect women and their children in this situation.
sentences.zh: 会将其视为一个里程碑式的事件，可能会为建立更好的体系提供动力，以在这种情况下更好地保护女性及其儿童。

sentences.en: A few of the things that are under discussion is, you know, there is active movement within the American Psychiatric Association to
sentences.zh: 目前正在讨论的一些事情是，美国精神医学学会（American Psychiatric Association）内部正在积极推动

sentences.en: expand its manual, the DSM, to include a chapter on postpartum disorders, you know, which would make it easier to identify and diagnose and treat them.
sentences.zh: 扩大其手册（即DSM）的内容，将关于产后失调症的章节包含在内，这将使识别、诊断和治疗它们变得更加容易。

sentences.en: There is a movement to get state laws that mitigate punishment in cases where a mother harms an infant in the postpartum period.
sentences.zh: 有一项运动旨在推动制定州法律，在母亲在产后期间伤害婴儿的案件中减轻惩罚。

sentences.en: And there is a long effort, really like a decades-long effort, to create specialized units where
sentences.zh: 经过长期的努力，实际上是长达数十年的努力，旨在建立专门的机构，其中

sentences.en: mothers in crisis can stay in a hospital with their babies until the danger has passed.
sentences.zh: 处于危机中的母亲可以带着她们的婴儿住在医院里，直到危险过去。

sentences.en: It sounds like perhaps another lasting impact of this trial, regardless of the verdict, is that
sentences.zh: 听起来，这场审判可能带来的另一个深远影响，无论判决结果如何，那就是

sentences.en: this conversation has been activated.
sentences.zh: 这场对话已经被彻底激活了。

sentences.en: All of these people have been activated and are talking about this in a way that kind of seems irreversible.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人全都被调动了起来，并以一种似乎无法逆转的方式在讨论这件事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样的。

sentences.en: I'm not sure you could put that genie back in the bottle.
sentences.zh: 我不确定你还能把这个魔鬼重新塞回瓶子里。

sentences.en: Well, Ellen, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 好的，艾伦，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: We're going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario,
sentences.zh: 我们将把安大略湖改名，

sentences.en: effective immediately to Lake America.
sentences.zh: 即刻生效，更名为美利坚湖。

sentences.en: On Thursday, President Trump followed through on his threat to change Lake Ontario's name to Lake America, a swipe at Canada and part of his escalating trade war
sentences.zh: 周四，特朗普总统兑现了他将安大略湖更名为美利坚湖的威胁，这是对加拿大的抨击，也是他不断升级的贸易战的一部分，

sentences.en: against one of the United States' closest allies.
sentences.zh: 矛头指向美国最亲密的盟友之一。

sentences.en: The Canadian officials have treated us very badly.
sentences.zh: 加拿大官员对我们一直非常糟糕。

sentences.en: They're nasty people.
sentences.zh: 他们是一群令人厌恶的人。

sentences.en: During remarks at the Oval Office,
sentences.zh: 在椭圆形办公室的讲话中，

sentences.en: Trump said that Canada was the worst to deal with on trade, and he re-upped a threat to slap steep tariffs on cars and trucks that are made there.
sentences.zh: 特朗普表示加拿大在贸易问题上最难打交道，并重申了对在那里生产的轿车和卡车征收巨额关税的威胁。

sentences.en: And emergency workers and helicopter crews desperately searched the Himalayan valleys for survivors after devastating floods swept through Nepal and Tibet.
sentences.zh: 在毁灭性的洪水席卷尼泊尔和西藏后，救援人员和直升机机组人员正拼命在喜马拉雅山谷中搜寻幸存者。

sentences.en: Nepali officials reported at least 389 deaths, with more than 1,400 still missing.
sentences.zh: 尼泊尔官员报告称，至少有 389 人死亡，仍有 1,400 多人失踪。

sentences.en: Survivors who spoke to Times reporters that traveled to the region described torrents of water that wiped out entire neighborhoods in a matter of seconds.
sentences.zh: 前往该地区采访《时代报》记者的幸存者们描述了洪水在短短几秒钟内吞没整个社区的惨状。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Alex Stern and Adrian Hurst, with help from Eric Krupke, Lexi Diao, and Ricky Nowetski.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由亚历克斯·斯特恩和阿德里安·赫斯特制作，埃里克·克鲁普克、莱克西·迪奥和里基·诺韦茨基协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Annie Minoff, with help from Michael Benoit and Chris Haxel, and contains music by Leah Shaw Dameron, Marion Lozano, Pat McCusker, and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 节目由安妮·米诺夫剪辑，迈克尔·贝努瓦和克里斯·哈克尔协助，配乐由莉亚·肖·达梅伦、马里昂·洛扎诺、帕特·麦卡斯克和丹·鲍威尔创作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由 Wonderly 创作。

sentences.en: This episode was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的音频工程由克里斯·伍德负责。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweth.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗韦斯。

sentences.en: See you on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 我们周日见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运转。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人热血沸腾的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我莎拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述那些试图维持自身影响力却在过程中失控的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何平台上收听。
